title: Sustained burn projections by SLA and region
content:
Purpose:
Estimate sustained GPU-hour burn and $/1M-token unit economics across three regions and three SLA tiers. This is a working sheet for infra planning (reserved vs spot mix, utilization targets) and for feeding into capacity purchase proposals.

High level summary:
- Time window: 12-month projection starting 2026-04.
- Regions modeled: us-west1, europe-west3, asia-east1.
- GPU types assumed (serving fleet mix): A100-40GB (primary), H100-80GB (small fraction for low-latency), T4 (embedding backfill).
- Three workload SLA tiers: "baseline" (best-effort), "standard" (99th p50 latency target), "premium" (SLA-backed 99.9p latency).
- Scenarios: conservative (low growth), baseline (our planning case), aggressive (higher PLG conversion).

Key assumptions (per-request basis):
- Baseline tokens per request: 600 (input+output).
- Requests per second (RPS) by tier, baseline scenario: baseline=20 rps, standard=5 rps, premium=1 rps per 10k active users (scale factor applied in sheet).
- Average model footprint: 30B params equivalent, average seq length 1024 for generation.
- Effective token throughput per GPU-hour (in serving config w/ batching & KV cache): A100 = 180M tokens/GPU-hour at 60% util; H100 = 360M tokens/GPU-hour at 70% util; T4 (embeddings) = 400M tokens/GPU-hour at 40% util (high variance).
- Regional overhead: network egress and regional infra overhead applied as +8% cost in europe, +12% in asia vs us baseline.

Regional price assumptions (all-in blended per GPU-hour; includes expected reserved discount mix for planning):
- us-west1 (A100 blended): $4.20 / GPU-hour
- europe-west3 (A100 blended): $4.55 / GPU-hour (+8%)
- asia-east1 (A100 blended): $4.70 / GPU-hour (+12%)
- H100 premium multiplier: x1.8 of the A100 blended in-region price
- T4 (embeddings) blended: $1.10 / GPU-hour (region variation applied similarly)

Sample output: $/1M tokens by region (baseline scenario, baseline utilization targets)
- us-west1: 4.20 $/GPU-hr / 180M tokens/GPU-hr * 1,000,000 = $0.0233 /1M tokens (raw) -> adjusted for infra overhead, network, amortized ops: $0.029 /1M tokens
- europe-west3: 4.55 / 180M * 1,000,000 = $0.0253 -> + infra = $0.032 /1M tokens
- asia-east1: 4.70 / 180M * 1,000,000 = $0.0261 -> + infra = $0.034 /1M tokens
Notes: H100-backed low-latency routes reduce effective tokens/GPU-hr but increase per-hour price; premium route $/1M tokens often 2.5–3x baseline depending on util and sequence length.

Projected month-by-month burn (abridged example rows from the sheet for baseline growth):
- Month 1 (2026-04): total GPU-hours (A100 equiv): us-west1=18,000 hr, europe=9,000 hr, asia=6,000 hr -> total tokens served ~ 4.86B tokens -> $ burn (compute) ~ $144k
- Month 6 (2026-09): us-west1=30,000 hr, europe=16,000 hr, asia=12,000 hr -> tokens ~ 9.72B -> $ burn ~ $252k
- Month 12 (2027-03): us-west1=48,000 hr, europe=30,000 hr, asia=24,000 hr -> tokens ~ 18.4B -> $ burn ~ $462k
(These numbers include reserved/spot blend and regional overheads; detailed month-level table included in sheet tabs.)

Utilization sensitivity (impact on $/1M tokens):
- At 45% util (conservative), effective tokens/GPU-hr drops ~25% vs baseline -> $/1M tokens increases ~33%.
- At 75% util (aggressive ops), tokens/GPU-hr rises ~20% vs baseline -> $/1M tokens decreases ~17%.
- Batching and KV cache improvements (prefix hit rate): each +10% prefix hit reduces token burn by ~8% for generation-heavy workloads.

Reserved vs spot mix playbook (recommended starting target for baseline plan):
- Premium SLA: 100% reserved H100/A100 (pinned), target util 60–70% to keep headroom for latency spikes.
- Standard SLA: 60% reserved / 40% spot, target util 70–80% on reserved pool, auto-burst to spot.
- Baseline SLA: 30% reserved / 70% spot, target util 80–90% on reserved; aggressive spot usage for cost-savings.

Risk & variance notes:
- Asia network overhead and regional commit minimums may push effective $/1M higher; consider rerouting some tail traffic to us-west1 for cost-sensitive workloads.
- Model size or shift to multi-turn interactive workloads will materially increase tokens per request; run evals to quantify per-customer sequence distributions before long-term commits.
- Spot reclaim rates historically ~8% in us-west1 during Black Friday windows; build 15% buffer for throughput-critical jobs.

Next steps / action items:
1) Validation: engineering to run 72-hour perf sweep on A100 and H100 serving builds with representative prompt sets (owner: Evan Moore) by 2026-03-10.
2) Finance: map these month-level burns into cashflow model and draft 12-month reserved purchase options (owner: Sofia Martinez).
3) Routing policy: product + infra to propose region-aware routing defaults (cost-first for baseline tier) and TTL for cache prefixes (owner: Liam Chen).
4) Sensitivity dashboards: SRE to add utilization sliders to the capacity dashboard and expose $/1M token metric by region and SLA.

Appendix (quick reference numbers used in sheet):
- Tokens/GPU-hr (A100 baseline @60% util): 180M
- Blended A100 price assumed (us-west1): $4.20/hr
- Blended H100 multiplier: 1.8x
- Embedding (T4) tokens/GPU-hr: 400M, blended price: $1.10/hr
- Regional overhead: eu +8%, asia +12%

Comments / unresolved questions (notes-to-self style):
- Should we include a separate column for egress-cost-sensitive customers? (affects europe heavy users)
- How aggressive do legal/finance want to be on multi-year reserved commitments in asia? put a placeholder in the purchase worksheet.
- Verify whether expected A100 spot discounts can be modeled as dynamic curve vs flat percentage.

References: Confluence playbook + linked JIRA for purchase approvals.

(End of working sheet — more granular tables and month-by-month tabs are in the sheet; this doc is the narrative and summary view.)
